PullRequest.Title: chat: Center code edit pill file icons
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- center code edit pill contents on the flex cross axis
- center the masked file icon independently of inline text baselines
- remove pixel nudges while preserving the existing contained, centered mask sizing

## Validation

- `npm run stylelint -- src/vs/workbench/contrib/chat/browser/widget/chatContentParts/media/chatCodeBlockPill.css`
- `npm run transpile-client`
- captured matching production-component fixture screenshots in Dark Modern with VS Code Modern Icons at 200% zoom

Fixes #334621

## Visual verification

Dark Modern theme · VS Code Modern Icons · 200% zoom · 704×222 fixture canvas

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| ![Before: masked file icons sit low relative to the labels](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7aa0a8eb-068d-41f8-8cc9-9c5102bd2c76) | ![After: masked file icons are vertically centered with the labels](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/46e428d9-1e31-43a4-9170-cd37339f5c20) |

Scenarios.Scenario: Streaming chat edit pills rendered for files modified by the chat editing pipeline
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Each code-block pill is created during markdown response rendering, then existing observable updates write status text, progress width, and classes while edits stream. The new inline-flex and align-items declarations participate only in the browser's normal style/layout pass; they add no JavaScript layout read or extra update and therefore do not create a new blocking step.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One pill per rendered edited-file code block; progress updates scale with the existing rewrite-ratio notifications for each actively edited file. The diff does not change pill count, notification count, or effective cardinality.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: DOM mutations run synchronously on the renderer/UI thread as before. Observable updates may cover multiple files, but there is no new parallelism, queue, limiter, or burst introduced by these static CSS declarations.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The stylesheet and computed-style machinery use normal browser caching. The change introduces no application cache, cache key, invalidation path, miss, or negative-cache behavior; cold and warm rendering differ only by ordinary browser stylesheet/style caches as before.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: the complete diff is static CSS, and the streaming call path contains style writes but no geometry reads in ChatEditPillElement; the change neither adds calls nor changes the progress update loop.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact pill counts and browser layout duration vary by response size and platform, but the changed declarations are constant-time per affected element and do not alter update frequency or require synchronous geometry resolution.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. Flex cross-axis alignment can affect normal layout calculation, but it replaces baseline/pixel-offset positioning without introducing repeated forced layout, animation, retained state, or scaling boundary work.

Scenarios.Scenario: Static external-edit pills rendered in grouped thinking/tool output
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Construction synchronously creates a small fixed DOM subtree and applies the shared pill stylesheet. The changed declarations only center existing children during the same normal layout pass and do not delay data retrieval or trigger new work after render.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One static pill per external edit item, potentially multiple files in a response. Cost remains one ordinary style/layout computation per existing pill, with unchanged DOM-node count and no newly repeated processing.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Parts are instantiated synchronously by the chat list renderer and may be grouped into a thinking part. The diff adds no asynchronous work, concurrency, coalescing change, queue, or backpressure behavior.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No application-level data cache is touched. Browser stylesheet/computed-style caching applies equally before and after; the change introduces no cache misses or retained cache entries.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence from the complete stylesheet diff and the traced ChatExternalEditContentPart constructor: rendering uses already-provided metadata and performs no filesystem, IPC, network, database, or subprocess operation.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Responses can contain varying numbers of edited files, but the diff adds only two static flex declarations to existing elements and removes two offsets; no superlinear or boundary-scaled cost is present.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression. The changed CSS does not increase render frequency, DOM cardinality, retained memory, or synchronous layout boundaries.

Scenarios.Scenario: Opening a streaming or external edit pill to inspect the resulting file or diff
Scenarios.CriticalPath: User activation may resolve the original text model to determine whether an empty original should open as a normal editor, then opens an editor. This existing asynchronous model-resolution step can be on the click-to-open critical path, but the stylesheet change does not introduce, move, or multiply it.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the original resource through ITextModelService.createModelReference before deciding whether to open a file or diff editor.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: At most one resolution for a clicked qualifying edit pill; none during pill rendering or progress updates.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same click handlers and model resolution existed before the CSS-only change with identical cardinality and placement.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: For qualifying pure-addition edits, resolution is awaited on the user click-to-open path before the editor opens.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Exactly one activation and at most one model-reference resolution per clicked pill; no operation fans out over all rendered pills or edited files.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: A single click handler awaits at most one model reference before opening the editor. No concurrency behavior is changed by the CSS diff.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Model resolution may be warm when the text model already exists or may require cold provider/filesystem work. Existing model-service caching and disposal remain unchanged; the CSS change has no cache interaction.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence: the transitive click paths were inspected and the only potentially expensive model/filesystem boundary lies in unchanged TypeScript, while the diff modifies layout declarations only.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider latency depends on resource scheme and model-cache warmth, but both the boundary and its scheduling are unchanged by this PR.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable performance regression because the only expensive boundary is pre-existing and unaffected by the changed styles.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed the complete one-file, three-hunk CSS diff and traced both consumers of the edit pill through creation, streaming updates, grouping, and activation. The change adds static inline-flex cross-axis centering and removes fixed pixel offsets; it adds no forced layout reads, update loops, retained objects, animation, boundary calls, or concurrency changes. No performance findings were submitted.
